data:
go-approx is the home of approximation in the parity plan: interpolation, splines, polynomials, and later Chebyshev and AAA approximation and scattered data.
Package Status Repository interp released v0.2.0 go-approx/interp poly released v0.1.0 go-approx/poly
data.what-is-verified#What is verified: From STATUS.md: numpy.interp, interp1d, PCHIP, Akima and poly1d are bit-identical to NumPy and SciPy; splines agree within 1e-15 to 1e-10. interp v0.2.0 adds Splrep (FITPACK’s legacy splrep) and is faster than SciPy on every case measured except two still open: RegularGridInterpolator linear evaluation at 10^3 to 10^4 points (0.95 to 0.98x) and shuffled-query cubic evaluation at 10^4 points (0.94x). The speed comparison with the Python reference is in interp’s docs/perf.md.
data.where-to-read-more#Where to read more: Landing: go-approx.github.io Documentation: go-approx.github.io/docs Organisation: github.com/go-approx

data:
go-bignum is the home of arbitrary precision in the parity plan: correctly rounded big.Float functions, number theory, and the Go oracle harness.
Package Status Repository bigfloat released v0.1.0 go-bignum/bigfloat
data.state#State: From STATUS.md: v0.1.0 is released: correctly rounded roots, exponentials and logarithms, trigonometric, hyperbolic and power functions and constants, and the Go oracle harness. Every function is at or below mpmath’s time (0.18–0.97x at 53–200 bits, 0.27–0.92x at 1000 bits; docs/perf.md), and the results stay correctly rounded against mpmath on 28 840 cases in six rounding modes.
data.where-to-read-more#Where to read more: Landing: go-bignum.github.io Documentation: go-bignum.github.io/docs Organisation: github.com/go-bignum
